ClientProfile.title: ClientProfile
ClientProfile.description: Represents a business client utilizing the FlexAgenda platform to manage their booking services and configurations.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ClientProfile entity.

name.description: The official name of the client's business or organization.

description.description: A brief description of the client's business or the services they offer.

contactEmail.description: The primary contact email address for the client's administration.

phoneNumber.description: The primary contact phone number for the client.

timezone.description: The IANA timezone identifier for the client's operating location (e.g., 'America/New_York'), crucial for accurate scheduling.

Service.title: Service
Service.description: Defines a specific bookable service or event type offered by a ClientProfile, including its default parameters.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Service entity.

clientId.description: Reference to the ClientProfile that offers this service. (Relationship: ClientProfile 1:N Service)

name.description: The name of the service or event (e.g., 'Haircut', 'Yoga Class', 'Consultation Session').

description.description: A detailed description of the service, visible to end-users.

defaultDurationMinutes.description: The default duration in minutes for a single booking of this service.

maxAttendeesPerSlot.description: The maximum number of attendees that can be booked for a single time slot of this service (up to 6 as per requirements).

isAppointment.description: Indicates if this service is a fixed-duration appointment (true) or a more flexible event (false).

isEnabled.description: A flag indicating whether this service is currently active and available for booking.

AvailabilityRule.title: AvailabilityRule
AvailabilityRule.description: Defines recurring patterns of availability for a ClientProfile or a specific Service (e.g., 'Mon-Fri, 9 AM - 5 PM').

id.description: Unique identifier for the AvailabilityRule entity.

clientId.description: Reference to the ClientProfile to whom this availability rule belongs. (Relationship: ClientProfile 1:N AvailabilityRule)

serviceId.description: Optional reference to a specific Service if this rule only applies to that service. If null, it applies to the entire client's calendar. (Relationship: Service 1:N AvailabilityRule)

dayOfWeek.description: The day of the week for which this rule applies (e.g., 'MONDAY', 'TUESDAY', 'ANY').

startTime.description: The start time of the availability period (e.g., '09:00').

endTime.description: The end time of the availability period (e.g., '17:00').

effectiveStartDate.description: Optional date from which this rule becomes active (e.g., for seasonal availability).

effectiveEndDate.description: Optional date until which this rule remains active.

description.description: An administrative description of the availability rule.

AvailabilityException.title: AvailabilityException
AvailabilityException.description: Defines one-off deviations from regular availability patterns, such as holidays or special events.

id.description: Unique identifier for the AvailabilityException entity.

clientId.description: Reference to the ClientProfile to whom this exception applies. (Relationship: ClientProfile 1:N AvailabilityException)

serviceId.description: Optional reference to a specific Service if this exception only affects that service. If null, it affects the entire client's calendar. (Relationship: Service 1:N AvailabilityException)

exceptionDate.description: The specific date for which this exception is valid.

startTime.description: Optional start time for the exception, if it's a partial day override (e.g., '12:00').

endTime.description: Optional end time for the exception, if it's a partial day override (e.g., '13:00').

isAvailable.description: If true, this exception adds availability. If false, it blocks availability for the specified period.

reason.description: A brief explanation for the availability exception (e.g., 'Holiday', 'Maintenance', 'Special Event').

BookingSlot.title: BookingSlot
BookingSlot.description: Represents a specific, bookable time slot for a Service, tracking its capacity and current bookings. These slots are generated based on Service properties and AvailabilityRules/AvailabilityExceptions.

id.description: Unique identifier for the BookingSlot entity.

serviceId.description: Reference to the Service this slot is for. (Relationship: Service 1:N BookingSlot)

startTime.description: The full date and time when this booking slot begins.

endTime.description: The full date and time when this booking slot ends.

totalCapacity.description: The maximum number of attendees this slot can accommodate (derived from Service.maxAttendeesPerSlot).

bookedAttendeesCount.description: The current total number of attendees booked for this slot across all individual bookings.

status.description: The current status of the booking slot (e.g., 'AVAILABLE', 'FULL', 'BLOCKED').

isBookable.description: A derived flag indicating if the slot can still accept new bookings (true if bookedAttendeesCount < totalCapacity).

Booking.title: Booking
Booking.description: Represents an actual reservation made by an end-user for a specific BookingSlot.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Booking entity.

bookingSlotId.description: Reference to the specific BookingSlot that has been reserved. (Relationship: BookingSlot 1:N Booking)

bookerName.description: The full name of the person making the booking.

bookerEmail.description: The email address of the person making the booking, used for confirmations and reminders.

bookerPhoneNumber.description: An optional phone number for the person making the booking.

numberOfAttendees.description: The number of people included in this specific booking, which contributes to the BookingSlot's capacity.

bookingDateTime.description: The timestamp when this booking was created.

status.description: The current status of the booking (e.g., 'CONFIRMED', 'PENDING', 'CANCELLED', 'ATTENDED').

confirmationCode.description: A unique, short code provided to the end-user for easy reference, confirmation, or cancellation.

notes.description: Optional notes or special requests provided by the booker.

definition.description: Documents indicating platform-wide administrators for FlexAgenda. Used for DBAC (Database Access Control) via existence checks, granting full privileges over ClientProfile creation and management. `uid` parameter refers to the unique user ID of the platform administrator.

Includes denormalized `clientId` and `clientAdmins` map (`{ [uid: string]: boolean }`) from the parent ClientProfile for authorization independence. `ruleId` parameter refers to the unique identifier of the availability rule.

Includes denormalized `clientId` and `clientAdmins` map (`{ [uid: string]: boolean }`) from the parent ClientProfile for authorization independence. `exceptionId` parameter refers to the unique identifier of the availability exception.

params.description: The unique identifier of the AvailabilityException.

definition.description: Generated bookable time slots for services. Denormalized `clientId`, `serviceId`, and `clientAdmins` map (`{ [uid: string]: boolean }`) from the related ClientProfile for authorization and efficient querying (QAPs). Publicly readable for end-users to find slots when `isBookable` is true. `slotId` parameter refers to the unique identifier of the booking slot.

Denormalized `clientId`, `serviceId`, `bookingSlotId`, and `clientAdmins` map (`{ [uid: string]: boolean }`) for authorization and efficient querying (QAPs). Booker can manage their own booking using `bookerEmail` (if authenticated) or `confirmationCode`. `bookingId` parameter refers to the unique identifier of the booking.

params.description: The unique identifier of the Booking.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure for FlexAgenda is designed with a strong emphasis on Authorization Independence, Structural Segregation, and consistent Access Modeling to ensure security, scalability, and debuggability. All authorization decisions are made without requiring `get()` calls to parent documents, thus enabling atomic operations and simplifying security rules.

**Authorization Independence via Denormalization:**
To achieve this critical principle, the `clientAdmins` map, which defines the administrators for a specific `ClientProfile`, is denormalized from the `ClientProfile` document into all its sub-entities (`Service`, `AvailabilityRule`, `AvailabilityException`) and directly into related top-level entities (`BookingSlot`, `Booking`). This means every relevant document contains the necessary authorization context (`clientAdmins: { [uid: string]: boolean }`) to determine if a `request.auth.uid` has administrative access for that specific client's data. This eliminates the need for `get()` operations in security rules when checking client-specific permissions, making rules simpler, more performant, and less prone to transaction-related issues.

For global FlexAgenda platform administrators, a dedicated top-level collection `/platform_admins/{uid}` is used. An `exists()` check against this collection (which is a form of `get()` for a global role) is generally accepted for high-level, infrequent permission checks and does not violate the spirit of avoiding `get()` for hierarchical data dependencies.

**QAPs (Secure `list` operations):**

1.  **`/client_profiles/{clientId}/services/{serviceId}`:** Public users can list services that are `isEnabled: true`. Client administrators can list all services associated with their `clientId`. The denormalized `clientAdmins` map ensures that rules like `allow read: if request.auth.uid in resource.data.clientAdmins || resource.data.isEnabled == true;` can be evaluated directly on the document without filtering sensitive data client-side. This ensures QAPs for both public visibility and administrative management.
2.  **`/booking_slots/{slotId}`:** This collection supports efficient `list` operations for end-users by denormalizing `clientId`, `serviceId`, and `isBookable`. End-users can query for `booking_slots` where `isBookable: true`, filtered by `clientId` and `serviceId`. The rule `allow list: if resource.data.isBookable == true;` ensures that only truly bookable slots are returned, adhering to QAPs.
3.  **`/bookings/{bookingId}`:** This top-level collection allows client administrators to list all bookings for their client (`bookings.where('clientId', '==', '...')`) by checking `request.auth.uid in resource.data.clientAdmins`. Authenticated end-users can list their own bookings (`bookings.where('bookerEmail', '==', request.auth.token.email)`). Unauthenticated users can retrieve a single booking using its `confirmationCode` for read access, but `list` for unauthenticated users is not supported for security reasons, aligning with QAPs.

**Structural Segregation:**
Each collection primarily holds documents with a homogeneous security posture. While `Service` and `BookingSlot` documents might have both public (`isEnabled`, `isBookable`) and administrative (`clientAdmins`) access requirements, these are managed by explicit fields rather than separating into distinct collections. This avoids over-fragmentation and simplifies data management while maintaining clear security boundaries via security rules.

**Access Modeling:**

*   **Client-Owned Data:** `ClientProfile` serves as the root for a client's specific data. Nested subcollections (`services`, `availability_rules`, `availability_exceptions`) continue the hierarchical path, making ownership explicit.
*   **Collaborative Data:** `clientAdmins` uses the membership map pattern to grant client-specific administrative roles.
*   **Global Roles:** `/platform_admins/{uid}` uses the existence pattern for platform-wide administrative privileges.
